title: Cheesy Lace
paragraphs: “What on earth is going on here!?”

I looked at the odds table displayed on Shieldfreeden. There’s a lot of technical jargon in this area, but as long as you understand the numbers and symbols, you can usually figure it out. So, regarding the issue, I stormed into Rival’s room—the event organizer’s room—to lodge a protest.
“This handicap is exactly what you said it would be. Honestly, I don’t think it’s any fun unless you go so far that even I can tell it’s overkill.”

That’s right—what I was pointing out was the massive weight overload caused by the huge handicap imposed solely on Yuki-chan. Anyone who looked at the odds agreed it was way too harsh—not just that they had no intention of letting her win, but an overload so extreme it was downright pitiful for Filolial-sama. When Yuki-chan arrived at the racetrack… she was saddled with a saddle and gear that looked like she was dragging several iron balls—the kind a felon would pull. With every step she took, I could almost hear her groans, thud, thud. Why does Yuki-chan, an Idol, have to look like this?!
“Yuki-chan isn’t a prisoner!”
“She seems to be walking just fine. The Spear Hero is just overreacting, isn’t she?”
Our Rival is abusing her power to bully Yuki-chan! I absolutely cannot forgive this!
“Hey, Gaelion-chan, I saw Yuki-chan at the venue earlier, but…”
Just then, Father showed up with everyone. Of course he would. Even he’d have at least one complaint if he saw that.
“What on earth is that?”

“It’s exactly the overload I told you about. With a performance like that, even those willing to bet would have their notions of special treatment—just because she was raised by a Hero—blown away. And while we’re at it, wasn’t she mocking those who worship dragons, too?”
“Well, yeah—I was even debating whether to bet myself.”
“And yet, you bet your entire recent paycheck on a single bet, didn’t you…”
Zou said with a look of exasperation. Panda… he actually bet on Yuki-chan, even after she was reduced to such a pitiful state. Well, I suppose the money was the real draw.
“Well, if I thought I could definitely win at those odds… of course I’d bet!”
Panda said this with more conviction than ever before. Is something wrong? It’s a given that Yuki-chan will win.
“Even after everything that happened, we still think we can win…”
Éclair seemed to agree as well.
“Don’t you all get it!? Yuki-chan’s cry from the heart! Her voice saying it’s heavy and painful!”
Since it’s a race, Yuki-chan has been made to run in the form of Filolial-sama rather than as the Queen. Putting something like that on Yuki-chan is nothing short of humiliation.

“She was walking with footsteps just like Elmero-san’s, as if the weight didn’t bother her at all, right? Though the commentator did mutter in horror, ‘She seems full of energy now, but who knows what’ll happen once the race starts.’”
“T-Shield Hero…”
Zou looks embarrassed.
“Ah, sorry. It’s just that the nearest footsteps sounded like that.”
“You’ve gone way overboard with the weight, no matter how you look at it!”
“This is the start of a blatant fixed race where the one who thinks they can win even with that handicap is the one who’ll grab victory!”
“You’re the one who’s blatant!”
“So Gaelion-chan knows who’s going to win, too, huh?”
“Well, of course. Gaelion has a solid sense of judgment.”
I couldn’t care less about your judgment. Naturally, even with a handicap like that, Yuki-chan is going to win.
“Still, I wonder if Yuki-chan will be okay… If she gets a leg injury or something, it’d be no laughing matter…”
“Exactly! If anything happens to Yuki-chan, I’ll kill you!”

“Spear Hero, think about it the other way around… Think about what will happen to Yuki’s popularity after she overcomes all of Gaelion’s interference and takes first place. Once she transforms into human form and sings and dances there, won’t she become even more popular than Gaelion?”

Ugh… Just imagining that scene made me feel exhilarated. Rising from an underdog situation to earn everyone’s respect through her own skill… that’s Yuki-chan’s rags-to-riches story, isn’t it? But, you see!
“When you say it like that, it feels like you’re just going along with it, and that’s unpleasant.”
“Either way, it’s about to start. Just sit back and watch with peace of mind. If she gets crushed by something this trivial, even the dragons wouldn’t think of Filolial as a nuisance.”
I felt like Father-in-law and the others let out a slight sigh.
“Looks like it’s going to be a turbulent race…”
And just as Rival and I were arguing, the race had already begun.

As for the result… it was Yuki-chan’s landslide victory. Yuki-chan, whose body was jingling with iron balls, seemed completely unfazed as she pulled several lengths ahead of the other participating monsters and crossed the finish line, leaving the crowd momentarily speechless. Yeeeeahhhhh, that’s right!
“You did it, Yuki-chan! You fought off Rival’s interference and took first place!”
Overcome with pride at Yuki-chan’s performance, I dashed onto the track and gave her a big hug.
“Kueeeeeee!”

Yuki let out a happy cry and jettisoned all her weights. They thudded into the ground one after another. As if to serve as proof, the weights Yuki had been wearing were carried into the stands so everyone could see them, and the audience collectively inspected them.

Incidentally, leading up to this race, poison was mixed into her water and meals, and she faced interference—such as sniper attacks—while racing. It’s unclear whether these were the work of the Takt faction or simply a sign of low morals among the Shieldfreeden crowd, but the culprits have been apprehended and are currently being interrogated.
“Well… I can’t help but feel like this was staged, but they’ve certainly taken great care to make it look genuine.”

“I suppose they’ve convinced themselves that it wouldn’t have meant anything without going this far, and that those who didn’t believe in the Filolial raised by the Hero are at fault… In a way, you could say this was a massive publicity stunt for the Hero’s power.”
“Exactly!”

After that, at the awards ceremony, Yuki-chan transformed into an angel and put on a show, singing and dancing while using the trophy as a microphone, sending the venue into a frenzy with an eerie atmosphere. And just like that, Yuki-chan became a celebrity in Shieldfreeden.
Hyahha!
“I did worry a little that we might lose, but it was a needless worry, wasn’t it? Though, we didn’t make as much as I expected.”

As night fell, we were holding a victory celebration at Siltvelt Castle—as if it were a wrap party—when Panda, who had bet his entire paycheck, said this with eyes shaped like gold coins, rubbing his cheek against the money bag.
“In the end, the payout is based on the total amount wagered. Still, I think we made a profit because we expanded the scale.”
“If you really want to make a killing, you’d have to pick the exact order of finish.”
I know all about this sort of thing from my experience training horses for the Filolial Race.
“I guess I can’t really make a bet that big, though.”
“But if I bet all of Lars-chan’s salary… what would I even do with that much money?”

At that moment, Father looked at Panda and muttered under his breath. Hmm… I suppose the amount does make me a bit curious. Panda receives a salary from Siltvelt. And since she’s Father’s guardian knight—as the Shield Hero—she receives a decent sum.
“Come to think of it, Lasa does save up money, but I have no idea what she spends it on.”
Zou then stepped in to back up Father’s question. Panda then furrowed her brow, clutched her money pouch, and glared at him. “I don’t need your money, you know.”
“That’s my business, isn’t it? It goes toward bar tabs, gambling, and debts for equipment.”
“I get the bar tabs, but was Larsa really losing that much?”
“To begin with, a knight in debt…”
Éclair is sighing.
“It’s not surprising since she’s a former mercenary, but even with all that money and status, can’t she pay it all back?”
“Shut up! It’s my business!”
“I bet she’s got some secret collection or something.”
“I-I told you that’s not it!”

Does that mean I hit the nail on the head? In other words, she’s running out of money because of cute merchandise. Yeah, yeah, I get it. I used to hunt day and night to scrape together money to collect Filo-chan merchandise, too.

“She probably doesn’t have that much money just for merchandise, though. I don’t know how particular you are about materials… though when it comes to gear, not just for me or Motoyasu-kun, but for everyone, Siltvelt should be covering those expenses anyway…”
I remember how you were blinded by greed when we went salvage hunting with your Older Sister. Isn’t it just that you simply love money?
“Anyway, I’m going to take a break now. I’ve got to feed my subordinates something good, after all!”
With that, Panda hastily handed off guard duty and went off to rest.
“…We do get meals provided at the castle, though. What are they up to?”
“I hear they’re carrying out their duties as soldiers. Perhaps thanks to Lars-chan’s thorough training, they’re very well-behaved.”
Zou replied. Incidentally, it seems the Shusaku clan representatives and others were also participating and enjoying themselves.
“…I wonder what Lars-chan spends her money on?”
“When someone acts that suspicious, you can’t help but want to know, can you?”
“Hmm… I wonder just how much debt she’s actually in…”
“Since I’m curious, would it be okay if I looked into it a little?”
“It might be something she’d rather not talk about.”
“True, but if there’s some reason she’s struggling financially, I’d like to help out a little… after all, she’s helped me enough that I feel that way.”
“Hmm, that’s just like you, Mr. Iwatani.”
As expected of Father—you’re so kind. I don’t know if Panda has some kind of situation going on, but if there’s a reasonable explanation, let’s give him some money.
“It’s all about money, everywhere you look.”
Father gives a wry smile at Rival’s remark. Is that really something you should be saying?
“Sorry, Gaelion-chan.”
“Don’t worry about it.”
“Father, instead of worrying about Panda, I’d like you to praise Yuki-chan more! If it’s about money, we’ll earn plenty more ourselves!”
Aren’t you forgetting what kind of party this is? This is a celebration to honor Yuki-chan, who thwarted the schemes of that foolish Rival!
“Let’s toast to Yuki-chan’s victory!”
“Yes, ma’am! Yuki is going to become an Idol who can run, dance, and sing!”
Yuki-chan said this with a very refreshing, lively expression. That’s Yuki-chan through and through!
“Then for the next race, it’d be great to go head-to-head with that ‘Spear Hero’ and his strange driving style—the one Naofumi and the others told us about.”
The moment Rival said that, Yuki-chan froze.
“I-I’m really looking forward to racing against Motoyasu-sama. I’ll drive… elegantly…”
I felt like the tone of Yuki-chan’s voice dropped just a little… but that must be my imagination! It’s just my “Drive Mode” and “Touring” modes kicking in. We’re going to pull off a one-two finish.
“Gaelion-chan, I really think you should skip that one, don’t you?”
“Oh? Alright then.”
“Have fun racing with Yuki-chan!”
“That’s fine as long as it stays personal. Otherwise, I think the race might end up with nicknames that don’t match our expectations… After all, reputation is everything for an Idol.”
“You hit the nail on the head.”

And just like that, the victory celebration that day came to a fun close. Of course, Filolial-sama sang and danced inside the venue to liven things up. Just what you’d expect from idols. I’m pretty proud of myself, too.
A few days later… Fans began pouring into the underground concert venue I’d prepared, all eager to see Yuki-chan. Now that’s what I call a success. HAHAHA, I can’t stop laughing.
“HAHAHA!”

Plus, thanks to Father’s help, fans of the other Filolial-sama have been gathering too, so her popularity is growing. Hehehe… Eventually, I’ll drive out the Dragon Promotion Faction and make the Filolial Faith the state religion of Shieldfreeden.
“Ah, Sakura-chan, are you going to see Melty-chan today?”
“Hmm? Is something up?”
While enjoying breakfast with Father and the others in Siltvelt, Father calls out to Sakura-chan. However, it seems he’s asking about a secret meeting between Sakura-chan and her Finacée.
“Well, there is something, but I didn’t want to bother Sakura-chan if she already had plans.”
“It’s okay—Mel-chan said she couldn’t play today because she had something to do.”
“In that case, I’ll ask you to come.”
“Okay!”

Ugh… Sakura-chan. Lately, she’s been visiting her Finacée so often that she’s ended up near the bottom of the Filolial-sama election rankings in Shieldfreeden. It’s strange that Sakura-chan—the alter ego of that world-famous idol, Filo—is ranked so low. We’ll have to hold a “Support Sakura-chan” event soon.
